_about: Visible copy of the Target dates view (/target-dates, spec 6.3). Drafts for Swann's approval (decision 1); British English, no dashes, the vocabulary of spec 13. Kind, status and bindingness words name what a row's record says and nothing more. The bindingness words come from src/lib/regulation.ts, so they are not repeated here.

copy.method: Each row is one line of a country profile's migration timeline, or one dated target of a guide the Atlas quotes: the guides a place issues itself and, for an EU Member State, the EU coordinated roadmap, which reaches it through membership and is drawn with an open marker. The kind of date and how binding it is come from the guide's own record or from an annotation checked against its source; where neither exists the row says not recorded, and nothing is inferred from a label, a posture or a year. Set in law means a binding instrument that is adopted or in force sets the date; set in guidance means published soft law or guidance does. A proposal, a withdrawn, repealed or superseded text, or a date whose status is not recorded, is filed under not recorded, so a proposal is never drawn as law.
copy.methodReread: The timeline lines of the {places} profile stay leads until they are re-read at their primary sources: preview builds draw them dotted, and the published view leaves them out.
copy.method2: The chart places a date at its month where the source names one, and in the middle of its year where the source gives only the year; dates before 2025 are drawn in the Earlier column and dates after 2036 in the Later column, and today is marked on the axis. The sentence above the chart names the earliest date from 2025 on, and earlier dates stay in the Earlier column and the table. Places are listed in alphabetical order, and nothing on this page ranks or scores them.
copy.sourcesProfiles: The migration timelines of {n} country profiles, each with its own sources on its profile page.
